projects.projectName: Vivli AI Form Check Validation & Agentic Chat Automation

Risks.riskDescription: The project has 49 days of planned work (PAT, Regression, Deployment, Hypercare) extending beyond the September 11, 2026 contract end date without a formal contract amendment or change order. This creates severe contractual ambiguity, payment milestone uncertainty, resource commitment risk, and potential legal/commercial exposure for both parties.

riskChain.rootCause: Progressive timeline extension through operational planning without concurrent contractual baseline updates. Historical pattern shows regression testing and extended PAT were added after project initiation without SOW amendment, and the same governance drift has recurred with 7+ weeks of post-contract work now planned.
riskChain.trigger: Contract end date reached without formal extension; PAT phase commences Aug 31 and extends beyond contract; Regression, Deployment, and Hypercare entirely beyond contract period; payment milestones tied to post-contract activities; resource commitments required beyond original term without formal agreement.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Contract extension not formalized for post-September 11 work.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Payment milestone uncertainty, resource continuity issues, quality compromise, and stakeholder impact across PAT, deployment, and hypercare.
riskChain.impact: Critical contractual ambiguity, delayed completion, payment disputes, and elevated legal/commercial exposure.

Risks.businessImpact: Project completion delayed to October 30, 2026; payment milestone delays for $60,500 tied to post-contract activities; quality assurance activities may be compressed; stakeholder confidence erosion; resource continuity risk beyond Sep 11.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: SOW contract end: September 11, 2026; WSR planned end: October 30, 2026; Schedule status: UNDER REVIEW; No formal extension documented; Remaining payment milestones: $60,500 tied to post-contract activities.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: This is the highest priority risk because it threatens the project's legal and commercial foundation. With insufficient remaining contract time versus required work, extension is operationally certain but contractually absent.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risk noted regression testing and extended PAT were added after initiation without SOW inclusion, creating contractual ambiguity and unplanned effort.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: The same governance drift pattern has already occurred historically and remains active in the current project, making recurrence highly relevant.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If not formalized immediately, the project faces escalating schedule, payment, resource, and stakeholder risks as post-contract work proceeds without coverage.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical governance drift recurred in the same client/project context with similar PAT/regression extension conditions.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Schedule status under review; post-contract phases already planned; formal extension status not documented; remaining payment milestones beyond contract period.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Without immediate contract amendment, contractual and operational disruption is highly likely before or at PAT/UAT transition.
Risks.mitigation: Executive escalation for emergency contract amendment approval; execute formal extension to at least October 30, 2026; revise payment milestones; document resource commitments; establish revised acceptance criteria and governance reviews.
Risks.recommendations: Treat as P0 issue; prepare amendment draft immediately; secure written commitments; establish formal change control; document governance lessons learned.

Risks.riskTitle: High-Severity Client Dependency Bottleneck Blocking Critical Functionality
Risks.riskDescription: Four high-severity client dependencies remain unresolved or in progress as of Week 12, blocking completion of critical functionality including chat-based escalation, Azure monitoring/alerting, dedicated automation testing environment, and Guru Card integration. These dependencies directly impact Sprint 5 completion, PAT readiness, and deployment feasibility.

riskChain.rootCause: Client-controlled readiness items were not delivered per SOW timeline, continuing a historical pattern of environment and dependency-related delivery blockage.
riskChain.trigger: Pending escalation requirements discussion; unconfirmed Azure monitoring process; incomplete automation testing environment; Guru Card fit assessment still in progress; Sprint 5 start and PAT timeline approaching.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Unresolved client dependencies block completion of critical delivery items.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: Sprint 5 delays, PAT readiness degradation, further extension beyond current planned end date, and incomplete operational readiness.
riskChain.impact: High schedule, quality, and operational risk due to blocked functionality and delayed validation.

Risks.businessImpact: Sprint 5 completion may delay; PAT start may slip; resource and rework costs may increase; incomplete functionality may reach PAT; deployment readiness may be impaired.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: WSR lists 4 high-severity dependencies: escalation requirements, Azure monitoring process, automation testing environment, and Guru Card fit assessment, all unresolved or in progress late in Week 12.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: Dependencies are client-controlled, high-severity, and unresolved close to Sprint 5 and PAT start, making them likely schedule multipliers rather than isolated blockers.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risk recorded Sprint 1 slipping due to broader scope and client cloud environment dependencies.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: The same dependency-led slippage pattern remains visible and unresolved in the current project lifecycle.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: If not resolved quickly, dependencies will continue to block Sprint 5 closure and PAT readiness, potentially extending the project further.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical dependency-driven schedule slippage has direct analogs in the current unresolved client/environment items.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Open high-severity dependencies; delayed environment readiness; pending client decisions; schedule already under review.
Risks.predictiveInsight: Client dependency delays are likely to remain a primary driver of critical-path slippage unless escalated immediately.
Risks.mitigation: Executive escalation to client leadership; daily dependency reviews with named owners; hard deadlines; documented workarounds; dependency risk register with escalation triggers.
Risks.recommendations: Invoke SOW client responsibilities; establish executive dependency governance; create dependency war room; document critical-path impact; consider partial scope delivery if needed.

Risks.riskTitle: Extended PAT Feedback Cycles Causing Sprint Capacity Erosion and Acceptance Delay
Risks.riskDescription: Multiple PAT early access review cycles are generating continuous defects and enhancement requests that consume subsequent sprint capacity, extend development duration, and threaten formal PAT/UAT sign-off timing. The feedback-driven process is improving quality but also creating schedule pressure and scope creep risk.

riskChain.rootCause: Iterative feedback-driven development with PAT early access reviews after each sprint is occurring without strict triage controls, response SLAs, or strong defect-versus-enhancement discipline.
riskChain.trigger: Sprint 3 PAT review overlapping Sprint 4; enhancement-marked issues; high UI/UX bug share; bugs raised for in-flight functionality; formal PAT period approaching without clear scope controls.
riskChain.primaryRisk: Feedback loops consume development capacity and delay acceptance.
riskChain.downstreamRisk: PAT duration extends, UAT sign-off slips, and downstream code freeze, regression, and deployment are delayed.
riskChain.impact: High risk to acceptance timing, schedule stability, and scope discipline.

Risks.businessImpact: Sprint 5 capacity may be consumed by feedback fixes; PAT may extend beyond planned duration; delayed sign-off may defer milestones; backlog churn and rework may reduce predictability.
Risks.currentProjectEvidence: WSR states PAT early verification feedback generated defects and enhancement requests; bug list includes enhancements, UI-related bugs, and bugs for in-flight functionalities; PAT period planned for Aug 31-Sep 18.
Risks.currentContextReasoning: The project is relying heavily on iterative feedback while already under schedule pressure, and there is limited evidence of strong triage controls to prevent repeated extension.

historicalCorrelation.similarHistoricalPattern: Historical risk noted delayed customer feedback could impact subsequent sprint validation and implementation.
historicalCorrelation.historicalReasoning: The project remains highly sensitive to client review timing and feedback volume, with the same validation dependency pattern recurring.

Risks.futureRiskProjection: Without tighter triage and response discipline, PAT feedback cycles will likely continue to consume delivery capacity and delay acceptance.
Risks.recurrenceJustification: Historical feedback-timing risk and current PAT review pattern both show recurring schedule impact from client validation loops.
Risks.leadingIndicators: Enhancement-marked issues; overlapping PAT reviews; high UI/UX defect volume; formal PAT duration already extended.
Risks.predictiveInsight: A quality-improving review process is likely to become a schedule risk unless feedback cycles are strictly governed.
Risks.mitigation: Implement defect-versus-enhancement triage; establish feedback SLAs; prioritize fixes by severity; formalize change control; reserve sprint capacity for feedback; time-box PAT cycles.
Risks.recommendations: Communicate triage rules immediately; define acceptance criteria; time-box PAT; automate regression where possible; create feedback dashboard; freeze non-critical scope.
